long_biography.plain_text:
Chris Ellis began in the British coal industry before working in exploration for Shell in southern Africa and CRAE in Western Australia. Senior roles with BP Coal, Agipcoal and the Stratford joint venture broadened his operational experience. He then became a founding member and executive director of Excel Coal, taking responsibility for the design and engineering of four mines before Peabody Energy acquired the company in 2006.

Ellis continued in resources as a director and substantial investor, helping develop tungsten and mineral-exploration ventures across several commodities. He also co-founded an impact-investment platform with Sandrina Postorino. After leaving Excel, he established the Rona Ellis Foundation, directing support toward children's education, poverty relief, women's empowerment, animal welfare and environmental conservation.

uncertainties.detail: Chris Ellis is highly ambiguous, but Robb Report explicitly identifies the source-context owner as the Excel Coal co-founder and Sandrina Postorino's husband. Group 6 Metals filings connect mining executive Christopher Ellis to both Postorino and his controlled maritime entity. Foundation and investment-platform sources reproduce the same spouse, mining and philanthropic anchors. Unrelated insurance, technology, media, aviation and property executives were rejected.

ASX filings use Christopher Ellis, while the source record and nearly all public biographies use Chris Ellis. Christopher is treated as the resolved formal first-name expansion for identity analysis only; no name-field replacement is proposed because the source's established display name is supported and no middle name was found.

Ellis has current impact-investment, property and philanthropic interests as well as mining exposure. Public filings most clearly quantify his mining shareholdings, controlled lenders and board mandates, supporting Metals & Mining as primary industry and Investor as the current relationship. No claim is made that every personal asset is mining-related.

The core wealth event came from a company Ellis co-founded after an established mining career, and no evidence identifies inherited core assets. Reliable sources do not describe his broader family-capital or financial starting position, so the origin remains broad Self-made rather than Independent start.

No reliable public source found in targeted research gives Ellis's date or place of birth. His British career start does not establish birthplace or citizenship, so no birth fields or secondary nationality are proposed.

The Rona Ellis Foundation's exact-person biography clears verification as an official company or institutional website. Its displayed LinkedIn link did not expose a distinct verifiable personal URL, and search returned numerous namesakes, so no LinkedIn or other personal social profile is proposed.

Vessel ownership, specifications, private homes, net-worth estimates, private asset values and time-sensitive project forecasts are excluded from both biographies. Private context appears only in identity evidence and uncertainty notes.
